title: Guest greeting standard
summary: Every guest is greeted within 10 seconds of walking in.
body_md:
## The standard
Every guest is greeted within 10 seconds of walking in, even if you are mid-cut.

## How
1. Look up, smile and say hello. "Hi, welcome in. Someone will be right with you."
2. If you are free, walk to the desk. Do not call across the salon.
3. Ask their name and use it. Check whether they checked in online.
4. Give an honest wait time. Round up, never down.
5. Offer a seat and point out where they can see their place in line.

## If you are the only one on the floor
Pause, greet, tell them the wait, and go back to your guest. Thank your guest in the chair for their patience.

## Never
- Let a guest stand at the desk unacknowledged.
- Say "we are really busy" as a greeting.
- Quote a wait time you cannot keep.

title: Consultation standard
summary: A two minute conversation before every cut, in the mirror, before the cape.
body_md:
## The standard
Every guest gets a consultation before the cape goes on. It takes about two minutes and it prevents most redos.

## The five questions
1. "What are we doing today?"
2. "When was your last cut, and what did you like or not like about it?"
3. "How do you style it day to day?"
4. "How short on the sides and back? How much off the top?" Show the length with your fingers or the guard.
5. "Anything else I should know? Cowlicks, a part, glasses?"

## Then repeat it back
"So a number two on the sides, blended, about half an inch off the top, and keep the part on the left. Sound right?"

Wait for a yes before you start.

## Offer the upgrade here
This is the moment to offer a shampoo. Not at the register.

## New guests
Ask how they heard about us and add a note to their profile so the next stylist can pick up where you left off.

title: The cut and finish standard
summary: What a finished haircut looks like before the guest leaves your chair.
body_md:
## The standard
A haircut is not finished until it is checked, cleaned up and shown to the guest.

## Before the cape comes off
1. Cross-check both sides for balance. Step back and look in the mirror, not just at the head.
2. Check the blend with the comb, against the light.
3. Clean the neckline and around the ears. Ask "squared, rounded or tapered?" if you did not already.
4. Dust off the neck, face and ears. Use the neck brush, then a towel.
5. Style it. Use product and say what you are using and why.
6. Show the back with the hand mirror. Ask "How does that look?" and wait for the answer.

## If the guest is not happy
Fix it now. No charge, no debate. If you are stuck, ask your manager or a senior stylist to look.

## Redo policy
Any guest can come back within seven days for an adjustment at no charge. Note it on the ticket so we can learn from it.

title: Salon appearance and cleanliness
summary: What the salon should look like at open, at 2 pm and at close.
body_md:
## The standard
A guest walking in at any hour should see a clean, bright, organized salon.

## Always
- Hair swept after every guest. No hair around the base of any chair.
- Stations clear except tools in use. No food or drinks on stations.
- Mirrors free of spots and tape.
- Towels folded and stocked. Used towels in the bin, not on the counter.
- Retail shelves full, faced forward and dusted.
- Front desk clear. No personal phones or bags in view.
- Restroom checked every two hours. Initial the log.
- Trash emptied before it reaches the top.

## Lights and music
All lights on during open hours. Replace bulbs the same day or open a facilities ticket. Music at conversation level, family friendly.

## Outside
Sweep the entry at open. Clean the glass door at open and after lunch. Report burnt out sign lights with a facilities ticket.

title: Uniform and personal presentation
summary: Black top, black apron, name tag. Clean, neat and ready.
body_md:
## The standard
- Solid black top. No large logos or graphics.
- Black, dark grey or dark denim pants or skirt. No rips.
- Company apron, clean and pressed. Replace it when it fades.
- Name tag on the left side.
- Closed toe shoes with a non-slip sole.
- Hair styled. You are the first example of our work the guest sees.

## Hygiene
Guests sit inches from you. Fresh breath, clean hands, light fragrance or none.

## Phones
Personal phones stay in the back room during your shift. Emergencies: tell your manager.

## Managers
If someone arrives out of uniform, handle it privately and help them fix it. Keep two spare aprons in the back.

title: Phone and check-in standard
summary: Answer within three rings. Every check-in confirmed by name.
body_md:
## Phone
1. Answer within three rings: "Thank you for calling, this is [name]. How can I help?"
2. Most calls are about wait time or hours. Give the current wait honestly and offer to add them to the list.
3. If you are with a guest, excuse yourself for a moment. Keep it under 30 seconds or offer to call back.
4. Never leave the phone ringing or off the hook.

## Online check-in
1. Check the list every time you finish a guest.
2. Greet online guests by name when they arrive: "Hi Maria, we have you down. You are next."
3. Take guests in list order. If you need to skip someone, tell them why.
4. No-shows: hold the spot for 10 minutes past their time, then move on.

## Walk-ins
Add them to the list in front of them so they see it is fair.

title: Wait time promise
summary: Honest wait times, updated every 15 minutes, and what to do when it runs long.
body_md:
## The promise
We tell guests the truth about the wait and we keep them posted.

## How
1. Quote the wait from the list, not from memory. Round up.
2. If the wait passes what you quoted, tell the guest before they ask.
3. Over 30 minutes: offer to text them when they are two guests away, so they can run an errand.
4. Over 45 minutes: tell your manager. Check whether anyone can be called in or a nearby salon has a shorter wait.

## What to say
"I told you 20 minutes and it is going to be closer to 30. I am sorry about that. Would you like to stay, or can I text you when you are up?"

## Managers
Look at wait times for Saturdays and the day before holidays each week and schedule for them.

title: Retail recommendation approach
summary: Recommend what you used and why. One product, in the chair, every guest.
body_md:
## The approach
We do not sell. We recommend what we used and explain why.

## In the chair
1. Tell the guest what you are putting in their hair and what it does. "This is a matte paste. It gives hold without shine, which is what you asked for."
2. Put it in their hand. Let them feel it and smell it.
3. Show how much to use and how to work it in.

## At the end
4. "Would you like to take the paste home today?" Then stop talking.
5. If yes, walk it to the register yourself.
6. If no, no problem. Note what you used in their profile.

## One product
Recommend one thing that solves the guest's main issue. Two at most. A list of five gets a no.

## Why it matters
Guests who take home what we used are more likely to like their hair tomorrow, and more likely to come back to you.

title: Local marketing and community guidelines
summary: What you can do in your neighbourhood, and what needs approval first.
body_md:
## You can do without asking
- Hand out referral cards to neighbouring businesses.
- Offer a first responder or teacher appreciation day using an approved offer from the Promos page.
- Support a school event with haircut certificates from your manager's monthly allowance.

## Ask your district leader first
- Any discount that is not on the Promos page.
- Sponsorships, banners or paid ads.
- Anything with our name on printed material you designed yourself.

## Never
- Make up a price or coupon.
- Use the brand logo on homemade flyers.

title: Shampoo and conditioner basics
summary: How to match the wash to the guest's hair and scalp.
body_md:
## Start with two questions
1. "How often do you wash?"
2. "Does your hair feel dry, oily or about right by the end of the day?"

## Match it
| Hair or scalp | Recommend | Say |
|---|---|---|
| Fine, goes flat | Volumizing shampoo, light conditioner on ends only | "This cleans without weighing it down." |
| Dry, coarse or curly | Moisture shampoo and conditioner | "This puts moisture back so it is easier to style." |
| Oily scalp | Clarifying or balancing shampoo, 2 to 3 times a week | "This resets the scalp without stripping it." |
| Flaky or itchy scalp | Scalp care shampoo | "Leave it on for two minutes before rinsing." |
| Color treated | Color care, sulfate free | "This keeps the color from fading between visits." |

## Tips
- Conditioner goes from mid-length to ends. Not the scalp, unless hair is very dry.
- Most guests use too much. Show them a coin-sized amount.

title: Styling products: which one and why
summary: Paste, clay, pomade, cream, gel and spray in plain language.
body_md:
| Product | Hold | Shine | Best for |
|---|---|---|---|
| Matte paste | Medium | Low | Short textured cuts, most men's styles |
| Clay | Strong | None | Thick hair, messy looks that need to last |
| Pomade | Medium to strong | High | Side parts, slick backs, classic looks |
| Styling cream | Light | Natural | Longer hair, frizz control, curls |
| Gel | Strong | High | Kids' styles, wet looks, very short spikes |
| Finishing spray | Light to strong | Low | Locking in a blow-dry, flyaways |

## How to show it
1. Rub a small amount between your palms until it is warm.
2. Work from the back of the head forward so the front does not get overloaded.
3. Shape with fingers first, comb second.

## Common mistake
Too much product at the front hairline. Show guests to start at the crown.

title: Men's grooming
summary: Beard, neckline and everyday styling for men's guests.
body_md:
## What men's guests ask about most
1. Something easy for the morning. Recommend one styling product, not three.
2. Beard care. Beard oil for dryness and itch, balm for shape.
3. Thinning. Recommend a thickening shampoo and a matte product. Shine makes thin hair look thinner.

## Beard trim add-on
- Offer it during the consultation.
- Ask where they like the cheek line and neckline before you start.
- Finish with a small amount of beard oil and tell them what it is.

## Say
"I used a matte paste today, about the size of a dime. It will hold all day without looking wet."

title: Color care
summary: Keeping color fresh between visits.
body_md:
## The three rules to give every color guest
1. Wait 48 hours before the first wash.
2. Use a color care shampoo and conditioner. Regular shampoo fades color faster.
3. Turn the water temperature down. Hot water opens the cuticle and lets color out.

## Recommend
- Color care shampoo and conditioner for every color guest.
- A weekly mask for lightened or dry hair.
- Heat protectant for anyone who blow-dries or uses hot tools.

## Book the next visit
Gloss refresh at 4 to 6 weeks. Root touch-up at 6 to 8 weeks.

title: Kids' hair care
summary: Gentle products and a calm visit for our youngest guests.
body_md:
## Products
- Tear-free shampoo and a detangling spray solve most parent complaints.
- A light gel or cream for school pictures and events.

## The visit
1. Greet the child by name, at their eye level.
2. Explain what you are doing in simple words. Let them hold the comb.
3. Clippers can be loud. Turn them on away from the head first so they hear it.
4. Take a break if they get upset. A calm two-minute pause saves the visit.
5. Finish with a sticker and tell them they did great.

## For parents
Show them how to detangle from the ends up. That one tip sells the spray.

title: Tools and take-home basics
summary: Brushes, combs and dryers: what to recommend and how to use them.
body_md:
## Recommend by need
- Vent brush: fast blow-dry, short to medium hair.
- Round brush: volume and smooth ends. Smaller barrel for shorter hair.
- Wide-tooth comb: wet hair and curls.
- Fine-tooth comb: parts and short styles.

## Show, do not tell
Hand the guest the brush for the last section of the blow-dry and guide them. Thirty seconds of practice is what sells it.

## Care
Tell guests to pull hair from the brush weekly and wash it monthly with a little shampoo.

title: Retail shelf standards
summary: How the retail wall should look every day.
body_md:
## Daily
1. Every facing full. Pull product forward to the shelf edge.
2. Labels face front. Price tags present and straight.
3. Dust shelves and bottle tops at open.
4. Promo product at eye level. Follow the current plan on the Promos page.
5. Testers clean, capped and marked "tester".

## Weekly
- Count the top ten sellers and reorder before you drop below three on the shelf.
- Rotate older stock to the front.

## Never
- Leave an empty facing. Spread the neighbours until the order arrives.
- Put damaged or leaking product on the shelf. Log it and set it aside for your district leader.

title: Opening the salon
summary: From unlocking the door to the first guest in 20 minutes.
body_md:
## Arrive 20 minutes before open
1. Unlock, lock the door behind you, turn off the alarm.
2. Walk the salon. Anything broken, wet or out of place gets fixed or ticketed.
3. Lights, music, heating or air on.
4. Count the drawer and confirm the starting cash. Record it.
5. Start the point of sale and the check-in screen. Check the online list.
6. Fresh disinfectant in every jar. Clean combs and guards at every station.
7. Towels stocked at stations and bowls.
8. Sweep the entry and clean the door glass.
9. Check the portal for today's announcements and promos.
10. Unlock on time. Not a minute late.

Complete the **Opening checklist** in the portal before the first guest.

title: Closing the salon
summary: Close out, clean up and leave it ready for the morning.
body_md:
## After the last guest
1. Lock the door at close. Guests already inside are finished properly, never rushed.
2. Run the end of day report. Count the drawer with a second person when possible.
3. Prepare the deposit and record it. See **Cash handling**.
4. Sweep and mop the whole floor, including under stations and the back room.
5. Clean and disinfect every station, chair, bowl and tool.
6. Start the towels. Do not leave wet towels in the washer overnight.
7. Empty all trash. Restock retail and back bar.
8. Clean the restroom.
9. Turn off tools, dryers and the sign as scheduled. Set heating or air to the after-hours setting.
10. Set the alarm and lock up. Leave in pairs when you can.

Complete the **Closing checklist** in the portal before you leave.

title: Cash handling
summary: Drawer counts, deposits, refunds and what to do when the count is off.
body_md:
## Drawer
- Starting cash is the same every day. Count it at open and at close and record both.
- Only people working the register that day open the drawer.
- Bills of $50 and above: check with the marker pen and put them under the tray.
- Never make change from your own pocket or the tip jar.

## Deposits
1. Count the deposit with a second person when one is available. Both initial the slip.
2. Seal the bag, record the bag number and amount.
3. Deposit at the bank on the schedule set by your district leader. Never keep deposits at home or in a car.
4. Vary the time you go to the bank.

## Over or short
- Recount once. If it is still off by more than $5, tell your manager the same day.
- Managers record every variance. Three in a month goes to the district leader.

## Refunds and voids
A manager approves every refund and void and writes the reason on the ticket.

## If you are robbed
Give them what they ask for. Do not argue or chase. Lock the door after they leave, call 911, then your district leader.

title: Sanitation and state board readiness
summary: General guide for California, Nevada and Arizona. Be inspection ready every day.
body_md:
This is a general working guide, not legal advice. Each state board publishes its own rules and they change. Your district leader has the current inspection sheet for your state.

## Every guest
1. Wash or sanitize hands before each guest.
2. Clean neck strip or towel for every guest. The cape never touches skin.
3. Tools are cleaned of hair, then fully covered in disinfectant for the contact time on the label.
4. Clippers: brush off hair, then spray disinfectant on the blades between guests.
5. Dropped tools are disinfected before they are used again.

## Every day
- Mix fresh disinfectant every morning, and sooner if it looks cloudy.
- Clean tools stored in a closed, labelled container. Used tools in a separate labelled container.
- Used towels in a closed bin.
- Shampoo bowls cleaned and disinfected after every guest.

## Licences and postings
- Every stylist's current licence posted at their station or the place your state requires.
- Salon licence and the most recent inspection report posted where guests can see them.
- State required notices posted. Ask your district leader for the list for California, Nevada or Arizona.

## Not allowed on the floor
Razor-type callus tools, nail work, or any service your licence and the salon's licence do not cover.

## When an inspector arrives
1. Greet them and ask for identification.
2. Call your manager or district leader right away.
3. Be polite and answer honestly. Do not guess.
4. Send a photo of the report to your district leader the same day.

title: Salon safety
summary: Slips, cuts, chemicals and what to do in an emergency.
body_md:
## Prevent
- Sweep hair after every guest. Hair on tile is slippery.
- Wipe up water at the bowls right away. Put out the wet floor sign.
- Cords off the floor and away from water.
- Closed toe, non-slip shoes.

## Cuts
1. Stop. Put on gloves.
2. Apply pressure with a clean pad. Bandage.
3. Clean and disinfect the tool and the station. Bag anything with blood on it.
4. Tell your manager and complete an incident report the same day, for a guest or for yourself.

## Chemicals
Safety data sheets are in the binder in the back room. Never mix products. Label every spray bottle.

## Emergencies
- Call 911 first for anything serious.
- Fire extinguisher is by the back door. Know where it is before you need it.
- Then call your manager and district leader.

## Working alone
Keep the back door locked. If something feels wrong, lock the front door and call your manager.

title: Inventory counts and ordering
summary: Monthly counts, weekly orders and how to keep shrink low.
body_md:
## Monthly count
1. Count on the date in the Operations calendar, before open or after close.
2. Two people when possible: one counts, one records.
3. Count retail, back bar and supplies separately.
4. Enter the count the same day.

## Weekly order
- Order from the order guide. Do not order outside it without your district leader's approval.
- Receive the delivery against the packing slip. Note shortages or damage on the slip and take a photo.

## Shrink
- Back bar product is for guests in the chair. Not for personal use.
- Testers are marked and logged.
- Damaged product is logged and set aside, not thrown out.

title: Scheduling and labour basics for managers
summary: Build the schedule from guest traffic and keep hours in line with sales.
body_md:
## Build it from traffic
1. Look at the last four weeks by day and hour.
2. Staff your peak hours first: Saturdays, weekday evenings, the days before holidays.
3. Post the schedule two weeks ahead.

## Watch during the week
- Compare clocked hours with sales in your salon page. Service revenue per hour is the number to watch.
- If the floor is slow, offer voluntary early outs in order of who has asked.
- If waits pass 30 minutes, call someone in.

## Fair is fair
Rotate closing shifts and weekends. Put requests in writing and answer them within three days.

## Breaks
Follow your state's meal and rest break rules. They are different in California, Nevada and Arizona. Ask HR if you are unsure.

title: Attendance and punctuality
summary: Be on time, call if you cannot be, and swap shifts the right way.
body_md:
## The basics
- Be on the floor, in uniform, ready for guests at your start time.
- Clock in and out yourself. Never clock for someone else.

## If you will be late or out
1. Call your manager at least two hours before your shift. A text alone is not enough.
2. If you cannot reach your manager, call the salon.
3. Out sick three days or more: HR may ask for a note. Sick leave rules differ by state. Ask HR.

## Shift swaps
Both people agree, and the manager approves it in writing before the shift.

## Missed punches
Tell your manager the same day so your pay is right.

## No call, no show
Missing a shift without calling is serious and is reviewed with your manager and district leader.

title: Respect at work: anti-harassment summary
summary: Everyone is treated with respect. How to report a concern and what happens next.
body_md:
This is a short summary. The full policy is in your employee handbook, which controls if there is any difference.

## Our standard
Every team member and every guest is treated with respect. Harassment, discrimination and retaliation are not tolerated from anyone: co-workers, managers, guests or vendors.

## What it includes
- Unwelcome comments, jokes, touching or advances.
- Treating someone worse because of who they are.
- Punishing someone for raising a concern in good faith.

## If something happens
1. If you feel safe doing so, tell the person to stop.
2. Report it. You can go to your manager, your district leader or straight to HR. You do not have to follow the chain.
3. Use **My Job > Ask HR** in this portal. Only HR sees what you send.

## What happens next
HR will listen, look into it promptly and tell you what they can. You will not be punished for reporting in good faith.

## Managers
If you see it or hear about it, you must report it to HR the same day. You do not investigate it yourself.

title: Social media guidelines
summary: Sharing your work is great. Here is how to do it right.
body_md:
## Go for it
- Post your work. Before and after photos are welcome.
- Tag your salon's city and say where guests can find you.

## Always
1. Ask the guest before you take a photo, and again before you post it. For anyone under 18, ask the parent.
2. Keep other guests and their conversations out of the frame.
3. Be yourself, and be kind.

## Never
- Post anything about a guest's personal information or what they told you in the chair.
- Share sales numbers, schedules or anything from this portal.
- Speak for the company or the brand. If a reporter or influencer contacts you, send them to your district leader.
- Argue with reviewers. Tell your manager and let them respond.

title: Tips, timekeeping and pay basics
summary: How tips are recorded, when you are paid and who to ask.
body_md:
## Timekeeping
- Clock in when you start work and out when you stop. That includes opening and closing duties.
- Take your meal and rest breaks. Rules differ by state. Ask HR if you are not sure what applies to you.
- Check your hours in the payroll app each week.

## Tips
- Your tips are yours.
- Card tips are paid through payroll. Cash tips are yours to take home and report.

## Payday
Pay dates and cut-offs are in the Operations calendar.

## Something looks wrong?
Tell your manager first. If it is not fixed by the next pay period, use **My Job > Ask HR** and choose Pay.

title: Guest privacy and information
summary: What guests tell us stays with us.
body_md:
## The rule
Guest names, phone numbers, emails and visit history are used to serve the guest and for nothing else.

## Do
- Lock the point of sale screen when you step away.
- Shred or return anything with guest details on it.

## Do not
- Copy guest contact details to your personal phone.
- Message guests from personal accounts about anything other than their visit, unless they asked you to.
- Share guest information with anyone outside the company.

If you think guest information was lost or shared by mistake, tell your manager the same day.

title: Employee handbook
summary: Where to find your handbook and who to ask.
body_md:
Your employee handbook is the full, official set of policies for your employer. This portal carries short summaries. If a summary and the handbook differ, the handbook controls.

## Where to find it
- You received a copy when you were hired.
- Your manager can show you the copy kept in the salon.
- Ask HR for a copy any time through **My Job > Ask HR**.

## Questions
HR answers handbook questions within two business days.

title: Your first 30 days
summary: What to expect in your first month, week by week.
body_md:
## Week 1
1. Paperwork and payroll set up. Bring your licence and ID.
2. Tour of the salon, tools and back room.
3. Shadow a senior stylist for your first two shifts.
4. Watch the Guest experience videos in SC Tube.

## Week 2
1. Take guests with your manager nearby.
2. Learn the point of sale, check-in list and how to ring promos.
3. Read and acknowledge the required standards in this portal.

## Weeks 3 and 4
1. Full guest load.
2. First check-in with your manager: what is going well, what you need.
3. Set a goal for service revenue per hour and product percentage.

## Who to ask
Your manager first. Then your district leader. HR for pay, benefits and anything personal.

title: Benefits overview
summary: A short guide to what is available and how to enroll.
body_md:
Benefits depend on your employer, your state and your hours. This page is a general guide. HR can tell you exactly what applies to you.

## Ask HR about
- Health coverage and when you become eligible.
- Paid sick leave. The rules are different in California, Nevada and Arizona.
- Product discount for team members.
- Continuing education and licence renewal support.

## How to ask
Use **My Job > Ask HR** and choose Benefits. HR replies within two business days.

title: Career path: stylist to manager to district leader
summary: What each step looks like and how to get ready for the next one.
body_md:
## Stylist
Great cuts, great consultations, guests who ask for you by name. Watch your service revenue per hour and product percentage on your stats page.

## Senior stylist or shift lead
You open and close, coach new stylists and keep the floor moving when the manager is out.

Get ready: complete the Leadership videos, close ten shifts without a miss, mentor one new hire.

## Salon manager
You own the schedule, the numbers and the team for your salon.

Get ready: learn the salon page in this portal, run a week of schedules with your manager, lead the morning huddle.

## District leader
You support six to nine salons and their managers.

## Raise your hand
Tell your manager or district leader you are interested. Nobody gets promoted by keeping it a secret.
